title: A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control
content: PubMed PMID 26551272. The SPRINT trial compared intensive systolic blood pressure control below 120 mm Hg with standard control below 140 mm Hg in adults with systolic blood pressure at least 130 mm Hg and elevated cardiovascular risk, excluding patients with diabetes. Intensive treatment reduced major cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality, but increased some serious adverse events including hypotension, syncope, electrolyte abnormalities, and acute kidney injury or failure. Relevant concepts: hypertension, high blood pressure, cardiovascular risk, stroke, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, CKD, adverse events, intensive treatment.

title: Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors with and without metformin: cardiovascular, kidney and mortality outcomes
content: PubMed PMID 33043620. This meta-analysis evaluated SGLT2 inhibitor trials and found reductions in cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, and mortality outcomes regardless of baseline metformin use. The evidence is relevant to type 2 diabetes, diabetic kidney disease, chronic kidney disease, heart failure hospitalization, cardiovascular death, kidney outcomes, metformin, empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, and SGLT2 inhibitors.

title: Inhaled Corticosteroids for the Prevention of Asthma Exacerbations
content: PubMed PMID 34400314. This review summarizes asthma exacerbation risk factors and the role of inhaled corticosteroids. It reports that inhaled corticosteroids are highly effective for preventing asthma exacerbations, with multiple dosing strategies including daily controller treatment, intermittent high-dose inhaled corticosteroids in selected patients, and as-needed inhaled corticosteroid use with rescue treatment in mild asthma. Relevant concepts: asthma, wheeze, exacerbation, inhaled corticosteroids, ICS, controller therapy, rescue inhaler, viral respiratory infection, eosinophilia.

title: Bleeding Risk in Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation Patients Receiving Direct Oral Anticoagulants and Warfarin
content: PubMed PMID 32676543. This systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies compared bleeding risk in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants and warfarin. Overall, direct oral anticoagulants were associated with fewer bleeding events than warfarin in observational data, with differences between agents: apixaban showed lower bleeding risk compared with warfarin, while rivaroxaban did not show the same reduction. Relevant concepts: atrial fibrillation, AF, anticoagulation, DOAC, NOAC, warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, bleeding, stroke prevention.

title: Risks and Benefits of Direct Oral Anticoagulants across the Spectrum of GFR among Patients with Atrial Fibrillation
content: PubMed PMID 30002224. This study evaluated direct oral anticoagulants compared with warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation across kidney function strata. It focused on bleeding and ischemic stroke prevention in people with and without chronic kidney disease. The record is useful for questions about anticoagulation when eGFR is reduced, CKD is present, or kidney function affects treatment risk. Relevant concepts: atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease, CKD, eGFR, kidney function, direct oral anticoagulants, warfarin, bleeding, ischemic stroke.
